overall: Atlanta is exiting a stormy overnight period with heavy rainfall and thunderstorms (90% PoP, 1-2 inches possible) that have kept temperatures elevated in the low 70s with very high dewpoints near 70°F. The running max is only 73.4°F as of 1:50 AM ET, but this is expected given the overnight convective activity. A post-frontal west wind shift is anticipated to drive partial clearing through the day, setting up a warm but not extreme afternoon ahead of a 30% afternoon thunderstorm chance after 2 PM.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP model agreement is exceptionally tight — ECMWF (84.8°F), HRRR (84.2°F), and NBM (84.1°F) are all clustered within 0.7°F of each other and closely match the NWS narrative forecast high of ~85°F. The INTRADAY bucket model shows a modal range of 86-87°F, running slightly warmer than the NWP consensus, likely reflecting uncertainty this early in the day (1:50 AM) combined with residual overnight heat retention from the high-dewpoint air mass.
max_temp_prediction: The dominant driver today is the balance between post-storm clearing (favoring heating) and residual cloud cover and high atmospheric moisture (dewpoint ~70°F) that will moderate daytime temperature rise. The tight NWP consensus centering on 84.1–84.8°F is the strongest signal, with the NWS forecast of 85°F as a round-number anchor. A slight downside bias exists given the heavy overnight rainfall that will leave saturated soils and potential lingering clouds into mid-morning, which could modestly suppress peak heating. Confidence is moderate-high given the strong model agreement; best estimate is 84.5°F, with meaningful probability spanning 83–87°F.
